summary: The additional proof inputs and analytic interfaces for RD.0: Laurent Fréchet charts and the Robba inductive limit, weak integral Amice topology and Frobenius substitution, valuation p-bases and overconvergent tensor descent, controlled weak lifting and endpoint homotopies, and Lazard divisor/ideal theory. The reviewed parent supplies the carriers and existing end targets. General smooth-algebra lifting, weak-completion invariance and completed characteristic-p fixed fields are precise lower-tier supplier requests.

nodes.title: Laurent Fréchet charts and the Robba inductive limit
nodes.statement: On the parent Laurent carrier define A_K(I) for a nonempty interval I of positive multiplicative radii by convergence at every radius in I. At radius ρ use |f|_ρ = sup_n |a_n|ρ^n. On each compact window J=[α,β] inside I use p_J=max(|·|_α,|·|_β). A_K(I) carries the separated complete topology generated by these seminorms and is their compatible projective limit; a compact I gives its Banach norm p_I. For a disc containing the centre use only n≥0 and include evaluation at zero. R_K is the parent union of A_K((r,1)), with the finest seminorm topology making all inclusions continuous. A cofinal sequence r_j increasing to 1 gives the same locally convex inductive limit (LF) topology. No strictness, bounded-set factorisation or completeness of this inductive limit is assumed.
hypotheses: K is complete, nontrivially nonarchimedean, of either characteristic.
Compact positive-radius annuli may have arbitrary real endpoints; no assumption that the value group is discrete.
The word locally convex is in the nonarchimedean seminorm sense; the pinned WithSeminorms API is used, rather than Mathlib’s real convexity predicates.
proofSteps: Use the parent coefficient carrier and convolution. Ultrametric summability gives the submultiplicative Gauss bounds; truncation by finite Laurent polynomials converges on every compact positive-radius window.

Construct the compact completion as weighted two-sided null sequences. Compatible coefficient limits on a countable compact exhaustion give completeness and metrisability of A_K(I); the topology does not depend on the exhaustion.

For discs use power-series truncations. Define the topology on the existing Robba union by all K-seminorms whose restrictions to every chart are continuous; the linear final property follows directly. Chart restriction is injective and continuous; multiplication is continuous on every fixed chart and separately continuous on the union.

nodes.title: Finite coefficient extension of Laurent and Robba rings
nodes.statement: Let L/K be a finite isometric extension of complete nonarchimedean fields. For every annulus interval I, the coefficient map A_K(I)⊗_K L→A_L(I) is a K-algebra isomorphism and a homeomorphism for the finite-dimensional tensor topology. A fixed K-basis e_1,…,e_d of L gives the inverse by taking the d coefficient-coordinate series. It also gives R_K⊗_K L≅R_L for the LF topologies and E_K⊗_K L≅E_L for the bounded-coefficient Amice norm topologies. No completed tensor is needed for finite L/K. Integral coefficient lattices are compared by uniform bounds; do not assert O_{E_L}=O_{E_K}⊗_{O_K}O_L without a separate integral-basis theorem.
hypotheses: L/K is finite, with its given norm extending the norm of K; this is coefficient extension, not the parent finite separable residue-field extension Γ_L/Γ.
No separability assumption is needed for this coefficient-coordinate argument; it applies in equal characteristic.
proofSteps: Read the finite-basis coordinate equivalence in Mathlib at the pin. Its coordinates and inverse have uniform norm bounds independent of the Laurent index.

Apply those bounds to |a_n|ρ^n at every radius, and to boundedness and the negative-tail limit for E. Reconstruct the inverse finite sum Σ_j e_j f_j and verify multiplication coefficientwise using convergent convolution.

Apply the same uniform bounds on every compact window. For the Robba union, finitely many coordinate series share a common inner radius; the final linear topology proves continuity in both directions.

nodes.title: The weak topology on the integral Amice ring
nodes.statement: For K a complete discretely valued field with integers O and uniformiser π, give the parent O_E the inverse-limit topology of O_E/π^m≅(O/π^m)((t)), where the latter has the additive t-adic topology: a series is small when every coefficient below a specified index is zero. Thus a fundamental neighbourhood of zero is U(m,N)={f: a_i∈π^m O for all i<N}. Equivalently f_j→0 iff for each m its reduction eventually has t-order tending to +∞. This topology is complete, Hausdorff and a ring topology, and is coarser than the π-adic topology. Finite Laurent polynomials are dense for it. The inverse-limit reductions are ring isomorphisms, not just bijections of coefficient sets.
hypotheses: K may have either characteristic; O is a complete DVR.
The coefficients of every O_E series are integral and tend π-adically to zero towards −∞.
For each m a reduction has only finitely many negative terms, but may have infinitely many positive terms.
proofSteps: Reduction of convolution is formal Laurent multiplication because only finitely many summands survive in each coefficient modulo π^m.
Choose compatible coefficient lifts in O to identify O_E with the inverse limit of these Laurent series rings. This proves completeness and Hausdorffness of the levelwise topology.

The t-adic multiplication estimates on each quotient give the ring topology. Truncate both tails modulo π^m to prove weak density. Every U(m,N) contains π^mO_E, so the identity from the π-adic topology to the weak topology is continuous.

nodes.title: Weak convergence of semilinear Laurent substitution
nodes.statement: Let σ_K:K→K be an isometric ring endomorphism preserving O and inducing q-power Frobenius on k, q=p^a with a≥1. For u∈R^int with u≡t^q mod π, the series Σ_i σ_K(a_i)u^i converges in the weak topology for every f=Σ_i a_i t^i∈O_E and defines the unique weak-continuous σ_K-semilinear ring endomorphism with t↦u. Modulo π its action on k((t)) is exactly the q-power map. It is π-adically continuous as well, but weak continuity is essential to its classification.
hypotheses: Mixed characteristic for the parent Frobenius object; the weak-convergence lemma itself also applies in equal characteristic when the stated coefficient lift exists.
u is overconvergent, not an arbitrary unit of O_E, when extending to analytic charts.
proofSteps: Modulo π^m write u=t^q(1+h) with h∈π(O/π^m)((t)). The inverse of 1+h is the finite nilpotent geometric sum. Positive powers u^i have t-order at least qi−C_m, since only powers h^j with j<m survive; this estimate is uniform in i.
For the positive tail use that estimate, including σ_K on coefficients; for the negative tail a_i vanish modulo π^m once i is sufficiently negative. Thus both tails converge in every quotient.

Use finite polynomial substitution and continuity to obtain additivity, multiplicativity and uniqueness on the weak completion. For reduction, raising a Laurent series to q in characteristic p applies q-power to coefficients and multiplies every exponent by q.

sources.match: Semilinear Frobenius and its levelwise topology; the quotient-wise substitution estimate spells out the convergence behind the displayed substitution.

For u=t^q the formula sends a_i t^i to σ_K(a_i)t^{qi}.
For K=Q_p and u=(1+t)^p−1 the reduction is t^p, although u is not equal to t^p.

nodes.title: Frobenius substitution and radius comparison
nodes.statement: Under weak-substitution-convergence, there is r_*<1 such that for r_*<s<1, |u|_s=s^q and |u/t^q−1|_s<1. If f is analytic at ρ=s^q and on a surrounding annulus near 1, its substitution is analytic at s and |σ(f)|_s=|f|_{s^q}. Consequently substitution maps A_K((r,1)) continuously into A_K((r^{1/q},1)) after increasing r sufficiently, and induces the parent extensions to R^int, R^bd, E and R. The radius threshold depends on u; it cannot be omitted or replaced by a fixed-chart endomorphism.
hypotheses: K is complete discretely valued with isometric σ_K.
The norm identity is asserted at radii of convergence, not for arbitrary coefficient families.
proofSteps: Overconvergence of π⁻¹(u−t^q) gives an exponential bound on its negative tail. Its positive integral coefficients and the factor π imply |u/t^q−1|_s<1 for all s sufficiently close to 1.

Apply the comparison of truncated naive partial valuations with the σ-defined partial valuations (Slopes Lemmas 2.3.3 and 2.3.5). This proves equality, rather than just the easy upper bound from submultiplicativity; it excludes cancellation between dominant terms.

Laurent truncations and the chart completion extend the equality to arbitrary analytic f. Uniform bounds on each compact window give continuity. Inverting π gives the bounded/Amice maps; the final seminorm topology gives the Robba map.

nodes.title: Valuation bases
nodes.statement: For a normed field F and a normed F-vector space V, an existing algebraic basis b indexed by ι is a valuation basis when for every finitely supported coefficient family c, the norm of Σ_i c_i b_i equals max_i |c_i|·|b_i|, with the empty maximum equal to zero. Use the NNReal finite supremum for this maximum. In additive valuation notation this is v(Σ_i c_i b_i)=min_i v(c_i b_i), with v(0)=+∞. This condition augments Module.Basis; it does not replace its finite-coordinate representation.
hypotheses: The uses here have ultrametric norms; the norm equality is meaningful on any normed space, and may fail there.
All sums are finite algebraic sums, not completed or Schauder expansions.
proofSteps: Use Module.Basis.repr to express the norm equality as a real-bodied predicate on an existing basis.
Translate max norms to min additive valuations by the fixed logarithmic normalisation. The zero family must be treated explicitly.
Transport the equality under reindexing and nonzero diagonal rescaling; each coordinate summand is bounded by the norm of the reconstructed vector.

nodes.title: Valuation p-bases and their finite monomials
nodes.statement: For a valued field κ of characteristic p, a subset S is a valuation p-basis when its finite-support monomials ∏_s s^{e_s}, 0≤e_s<p, form an algebraic valuation basis of κ over the Frobenius-image subfield κ^p. The empty monomial is 1. Coordinates have finite support in this monomial index set, even if S is infinite; each coefficient lies in κ^p. Equivalently, every x has a unique finite expansion and its valuation is the minimum of the valuations of its nonzero summands.
hypotheses: p is prime and κ has characteristic p.
κ^p is the image subfield of x↦x^p, carrying the restricted valuation; S contains no zero element.
proofSteps: Index monomials by finitely supported functions S→{0,…,p−1}. Use the existing basis carrier together with valuation-basis, requiring its vectors to be exactly these monomial products.
Uniqueness and spanning are algebraic requirements independent of norm orthogonality. Iterating Frobenius gives the analogous q^n monomial bases over κ^{q^n}.
Use the valuation formula to identify coordinate projections as nonexpanding on weighted summands, which is the ingredient of Lemma 2.2.19.

sources.match: Finite monomials, finite algebraic coordinates and the minimum valuation formula.

acceptance: An ordinary p-basis is insufficient without the valuation minimum formula.

nodes.title: The Laurent example with finite coefficient p-rank
nodes.statement: If k has a finite p-basis B, then {t}∪B is a valuation p-basis of κ=k((t)) with its t-adic valuation. This includes arbitrary perfect k, whose p-basis is empty. Without the finite-p-rank hypothesis, this particular monomial family need not be an algebraic basis of k((t)); the theorem does not assert that no other valuation p-basis exists.
hypotheses: k has characteristic p, and B is an ordinary finite p-basis of k.
The valuation on k is trivial and the valuation on κ is t-adic.
proofSteps: First split Laurent exponents into the p residue classes modulo p.

Expand every coefficient in the same finite collection of p-monomials in B. Each coordinate is then a Laurent series in t^p with coefficients in k^p, hence lies in κ^p. Uniqueness follows coefficientwise.

At the lowest t-degree, independence of the constant p-monomials prevents cancellation, proving the minimum valuation formula. The infinite coefficient example in the tests fails the finite-support requirement and corrects the source’s unrestricted example.

nodes.title: Projection from perfected Cohen coefficients
nodes.statement: For the parent Cohen/Frobenius data Γ, assume enough r_0-units and an actual valuation p-basis of its complete residue field κ. Choose unit lifts in Γ_{r_0} of the p-basis. There is a Γ-linear retraction f:Γ^perf→Γ, compatible with the coefficient-of-one maps on every σ^{-n} level, continuous for the levelwise topology, and carrying Γ^perf_con into Γ_con. On a sufficiently small common radius, it maps (Γ^{σ^{-n}})_r into Γ_r for all n and 0<r≤r_0, and the same estimate passes to the completed perfect coefficient ring. This is a linear projection depending on chosen lifts; neither a ring map nor a canonical Frobenius-equivariant map is asserted.
hypotheses: Γ, O, π, σ and the embedding in perfected ramified Witt coefficients are exactly parent analytic-ring; the residue field κ is complete.
Enough units supplies the unit lifts at a single radius shared by all p-basis elements.
Γ^perf uses the valuation-completed perfect residue field. The union of σ^{-n} levels is levelwise dense; do not claim it is π-adically dense after completion of the residue field.
proofSteps: Iterate the finite p-monomial basis. At level n use 1 and the fractional monomials first appearing in each level up to n (exponents not all divisible by q). Lift them using σ^{-n}. Their residues form a valuation basis over κ.

Successive reduction modulo π gives a unique restricted sum Σ_u x_u u, x_u∈Γ, with finitely many coefficients nonzero modulo each π^m at a fixed algebraic level. Send this sum to x_1. The maps agree on inclusions and are Γ-linear retractions.

Induct on the π-length to prove the truncated equality min_{j≤m}v_{j,r}(x)=min_u min_{j≤m}v_{j,r}(x_u u). It bounds the coefficient-of-one projection uniformly in the level, proves preservation of every sufficiently small shared Γ_r, and gives levelwise continuity.

Approximate the first finitely many residue coefficients in the completed perfect field by algebraic perfection levels; completeness of Γ for its levelwise topology extends f. Use the same truncated estimates before passing to limits, then all m, to preserve the overconvergence growth condition.

nodes.title: Galois-fixed completed overconvergent coefficients
nodes.statement: For the parent ramified Witt coefficients over the valuation-completed algebraic closure κ^alg of a complete characteristic-p field κ, let κ^perf be its completed perfection and G=Gal(κ^alg/κ^perf). Then (Γ^alg)^G=Γ^perf and (Γ^alg_con)^G=Γ^perf_con. Consequently an element of Γ^alg_con fixed by all Galois automorphisms is a perfected overconvergent coefficient. The completion in κ^alg is indispensable; algebraic fixed-field theory alone does not prove this claim.

The lower-tier completed characteristic-p fixed-field contract is supplied by PerfectoidSpaces:P3, as requested here.

This identifies the fixed field of the completed algebraic closure with the complete perfect base.

Witt functoriality acts coefficientwise. Uniqueness of the π-Teichmüller expansion, with G fixing π, makes every expansion coefficient fixed, hence in κ^perf. Conversely all such coefficients are fixed.
The valuations of these coefficients are their restricted valuations in κ^alg. The same partial-valuation growth test therefore identifies the intersection with the overconvergent subring.

nodes.title: Injectivity and coefficient descent after overconvergent base change
nodes.statement: Assume the parent Γ has enough units and its complete residue field κ has a valuation p-basis. Multiplication μ:Γ⊗_{Γ_con}Γ^alg_con→Γ^alg is injective. More precisely, for x_1,…,x_n∈Γ independent over Γ_con and y_i∈Γ^alg_con: Σ_i x_i y_i=0 forces every y_i=0; and Σ_i x_i y_i∈Γ forces every y_i∈Γ_con. These statements also hold after inverting π, with the corresponding fraction fields. No unconditional removal of the valuation-p-basis hypothesis is claimed.
hypotheses: The tensor product is algebraic. Γ^alg denotes completed algebraic residue coefficients, not the uncompleted algebraic union.
Γ_con is the parent henselian DVR with uniformiser π.
proofSteps: Choose a shortest nonzero relation among independent x_i. Divide by a coefficient of minimal π-valuation, so its new coefficient is 1 and the others remain in Γ^alg_con. Subtract every Galois conjugate; minimality forces the remaining coefficients to be fixed. Apply overconvergent-galois-fixed-coefficients.

Apply the Γ-linear projection. Subtracting its image yields a relation with the first coefficient zero, so minimality forces y_i=f(y_i)∈Γ_con. This contradicts independence. For a sum in Γ, first subtract its Galois conjugates, then its projection; the just-proved independence case forces descent of every coefficient.

For a tensor in the kernel choose a shortest presentation. The preceding result implies the x_i are dependent. Since Γ_con is a DVR, divide a nonzero relation by its common π-power and select a unit coefficient, expressing one x_i as a Γ_con-linear combination of the others. Rewrite x_1⊗y_1 as Σ_{i≥2}x_i⊗c_i y_1, giving fewer terms and a contradiction.

Localising at π is exact; clear finitely many denominators to obtain the fraction-field version. The Section 7.5 use is the injectivity of a base-changed map and descent of coordinates of a rank-one preimage; no new full-faithfulness target is planned in RD.0.

nodes.title: Controlled lifting from a smooth weak completion
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete DVR, S a smooth finitely presented O-algebra, and B,C weakly complete finitely generated O-algebras in the F1 sense. Given a surjection p:B→C, a map φ:S†→C, and a reduction map h̄:S/πS→B/πB with p̄h̄=φ̄, there exists h:S†→B reducing to h̄ and satisfying ph=φ. In particular every reduction map S/πS→B/πB lifts, by taking C=0. No uniqueness is asserted, and ordinary formal smoothness alone is insufficient for a nonnilpotent kernel.
hypotheses: O may have either characteristic for this algebraic weak-lifting result. Rational de Rham integration below requires mixed characteristic.
S† and the weakly complete algebra carriers are imported from F1.
The general controlled étale-neighbourhood theorem and weak-completion invariance are the exact SF.0 and F1 requests in this packet.
proofSteps: Restrict φ and h̄ to S. Apply the requested Arabia 2.1.2(b) controlled lifting theorem: a complete-intersection étale neighbourhood B→B_ε of (πB)·ker p has a genuine S-map satisfying both conditions.

This neighbourhood is canonically unchanged modulo π, because its defining neighbourhood ideal is contained in πB. It is flat and finitely presented over B. The requested F1 extension of weak completion identifies (B_ε)† with B and keeps the maps to C compatible.

Use F1 weak-completion functoriality to extend the S-map to S†. Check the two equations by their restrictions and reduction. The C=0 specialization is precisely the requested 2.1.3 reduction-lifting case.

For the parent semilinear Frobenius target, apply this linear result to the coefficient-twisted source over σ_O; then use the parent finiteness/flatness input. No assumption that σ_O is an automorphism is inserted.

nodes.title: Lifting a reduction homotopy with fixed endpoints
nodes.statement: Let O,S,B be as in controlled-weak-smooth-lifting. Given u_0,u_1:S†→B and a polynomial reduction homotopy h̄:S/πS→(B/πB)[T] with evaluations ū_0,ū_1, there is h:S†→B⟨T⟩† reducing to h̄ and evaluating exactly to u_0,u_1. Here B⟨T⟩† is the F1 weak polynomial extension, not B[[T]] or B⟨T⟩. If the reductions are equal, a constant reduction homotopy recovers the parent equal-reduction result; general homotopic reductions are the additional interface here.
hypotheses: S is smooth finitely presented over the complete DVR O; B is weakly complete finitely generated.
A polynomial homotopy of the reductions is part of the input; arbitrary reduction maps need not be homotopic.
proofSteps: On B[T], the joint endpoint map to B×B is surjective with kernel T(T−1). This follows from the coprimality of T and T−1 over every commutative ring; zero divisors in B do not invalidate it.
Apply the requested SF.0 controlled endpoint theorem (Arabia 2.2.2), whose étale-neighbourhood ideal is πT(T−1), keeping both endpoint maps and the reduction homotopy.

Pass to the weak polynomial extension using the requested F1 invariance. It is unchanged modulo π, and its endpoint maps are the F1 evaluations at 0 and 1. The resulting map therefore preserves both endpoints exactly.
For rational de Rham cohomology, compose h with rational-dagger-interval-integration; this gives the parent chain homotopy and identifies the induced cohomology maps.

nodes.title: Rational integration in a dagger interval
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete DVR of mixed characteristic (0,p), K its fraction field, and B a weakly complete finitely generated O-algebra. On the rational dagger de Rham complex of B⟨T⟩†[1/π], write forms with dT on the left as α(T)+dT∧β(T). Define the degree −1 K-linear operator H by integrating β(T) coefficientwise from 0 to 1; H(Σ_n b_n T^n dT)=Σ_n b_n/(n+1). It lands in the de Rham complex of B[1/π] and satisfies dH+Hd=ev_1−ev_0. For any fringe radius R>1 in T and the coefficient variables, choose a strictly smaller radius R′>1: integer denominators grow at most polynomially, so integration remains overconvergent on this smaller fringe. This is rational integration, not an O-linear integral-valued operator.
hypotheses: Use F1 dagger differentials and dagger de Rham complex on the rational generic fibre; a chosen finite weak presentation supplies the coefficient fringe.
For integers n≥1, |n⁻¹|≤n^c where c=−log_p|p|>0; this follows from |n|=|p|^{v_p(n)}.
Shrink the joint fringe when needed; do not demand bounded integration on the same fringe.
proofSteps: In a finite weak presentation, coefficient series have exponential decay in total degree. Since v_p(n+1)≤log_p(n+1), division by n+1 has only polynomial growth. The factor (R′/R)^n absorbs it, proving convergence and presentation-independent descent of the coefficientwise integral.
Prove the fundamental theorem coefficientwise on polynomials, with the stated dT-left convention, then use the growth bound to pass to dagger series.
The integration commutes with maps of B and with its differential in the graded identity. Composing H with an endpoint homotopy gives a chain homotopy between the two rational de Rham maps.

nodes.title: Compact Laurent preparation over arbitrary complete coefficients
nodes.statement: For a complete nontrivially nonarchimedean K and a nonempty compact positive-radius annulus J, every nonzero f∈A_K(J) factors as f=P u, where P∈K[T] is the monic polynomial whose roots, with multiplicity, are exactly the zeros of f on that annulus and u is a unit in A_K(J). A power of T is absorbed in u on an annulus. On a compact disc containing zero, P also includes the zero at the centre, which cannot be absorbed in a unit. Thus A_K(J) is a principal ideal domain. Newton break radii, finite polynomial factors and invertibility are characterised on J. These statements hold in equal characteristic and without spherical completeness.
hypotheses: Use the parent Laurent coefficients and laurent-topology-interface, not a second analytic carrier.
Zeros can be expressed through irreducible polynomial factors and finite extension evaluation; in characteristic p separability is not assumed.
Compact intervals may be singletons and need not be aligned with the value group.
proofSteps: At a radius, identify the finite block between smallest and largest dominant Laurent indices. Iterative ultrametric division factors the corresponding polynomial and a unit; completeness controls the successive corrections (Lazard Propositions 2–3).

On a compact window there are finitely many Newton breaks. Assemble their relatively prime polynomial factors; divide out the finite zero divisor and use the dominant-term inverse criterion for the remaining unit. For a disc include the centre order separately.

Lazard Proposition 4’s division/gcd argument gives principal ideals; factorisation also identifies a compact ideal generator with its finite divisor. The generic coefficient result is a new extension of the parent Γ-interval theorem, whose coefficient O is discretely valued.

sources.match: Newton polynomial/unit factorisation and compact division/PID theory over a complete field.
Compact annulus rings are principal ideal domains.
Arbitrary complete coefficient fields suffice on compact intervals.

acceptance: On an annulus t is a unit; on a disc containing zero it has a simple zero.

nodes.title: Effective analytic divisors over the coefficient field
nodes.statement: Fix a connected nonempty annulus or disc domain U and its Laurent chart A_K(U). Its closed analytic points are the monic irreducible polynomials P over K whose roots have a radius in U, with P=T included precisely when the centre belongs to U. Define an effective divisor D as a function from these points to N with locally finite support: on every compact subdomain J⊆U, only finitely many P have D(P)>0. The finite degree-weighted sum on J records geometric multiplicity. For nonzero f, div(f)(P) is the largest m for which P^m divides f near this point; compact preparation makes it well-defined and locally finite. Zero has no effective finite-multiplicity divisor. In characteristic zero this agrees with G_K-invariant locally finite geometric zero divisors, with degree multiplicities; in characteristic p use the irreducible-point form to retain inseparable multiplicities.
hypotheses: K is complete, nontrivially nonarchimedean, of either characteristic.
Every irreducible P has a single root radius, by the unique extended absolute value on a finite extension.
Polynomial multiplicity at a closed point is distinguished from geometric multiplicity after inseparable extension.
proofSteps: Use existing polynomial irreducibility and the unique extension of the norm, rather than importing a new space of geometric points.
Compact preparation identifies the local factor order and proves consistency under restricting compact windows. A compact exhaustion gives the global divisor and local finiteness.
Define addition and pointwise minimum; restrict by retaining points in the smaller domain. Verify the geometric comparison over characteristic-zero coefficients by finite Galois orbits.

nodes.title: Analytic principal parts and jet interpolation
nodes.statement: For a locally finite effective divisor D on U over any complete nonarchimedean K, arbitrary finite jet data at its closed points are realised by a global analytic g∈A_K(U): for every point P with D(P)>0, the image of g in K[T]/(P^{D(P)}) equals the specified residue class. Equivalently meromorphic principal parts with locally finite poles admit a global meromorphic realisation. This interpolation implies that every finitely generated ideal of A_K(U) is closed, whether or not K is spherically complete.
hypotheses: No uniform bound on the jets is imposed. This is interpolation without a growth bound, unlike spherical prescribed-divisor realization.
For inseparable P use the polynomial jet quotient, not derivative data at distinct roots.
proofSteps: Group the poles by packets escaping every compact subdomain. Each rational principal part whose poles lie outside a fixed compact window has a convergent power or inverse-power expansion there. Subtract a finite Laurent-polynomial truncation to make its norm arbitrarily small on that window. Summing the corrected packets converges on every compact window and retains all principal parts.

Choose the nonzero divisor majorant f. Extend the requested jets to orders div(f), including arbitrary zero data at the additional zeros of f. Apply the principal-parts construction to their local quotients by f; multiply the resulting meromorphic function by f to obtain a global analytic function with the required jets (Lazard (8.11)).

For generators f_0,…,f_m and g vanishing along their common divisor, compact division gives local coefficients on each circle. Interpolate the coefficients for i>0 modulo the zero divisor of f_0. The remaining difference is globally divisible by f_0, so g is in the generated ideal. This identifies the ideal with its closed divisor ideal.

nodes.title: Closed ideals and effective analytic divisors
nodes.statement: For any complete nonarchimedean K, the nonzero closed ideals of A_K(U) correspond order-reversingly to effective locally finite divisors on U. The zero ideal is an additional closed ideal, with no finite-multiplicity divisor. The unit ideal corresponds to D=0. On compact U every such ideal is principal; on noncompact U principality requires the separate spherical-completeness theorem.

proofSteps: Choose a nonzero member of I; its divisor bounds D_I, proving local finiteness. Vanishing to a given order is a closed condition on every compact chart, so I_D is closed. The divisor-majorant theorem supplies a nonzero member.

On a compact window, select finitely many members of I which attain the minimum at each of its finitely many relevant points. Compact PID theory produces their gcd on that window. Laurent-polynomial approximation to the local coefficients makes I dense in every function vanishing along D_I.

nodes.title: Prescribing exact zeros under spherical completeness
nodes.statement: If K is spherically complete, every locally finite effective divisor D on a connected annulus or disc U is div(f) for some nonzero analytic f. The stronger construction includes Lazard’s norm-controlled finite-zero interpolation on increasing compact windows. Conversely, exact realization of every divisor on an open disc detects spherical completeness; completeness alone does not imply it. Spherical completeness means that every nested family of nonempty closed balls in K has nonempty intersection.

The inverse implication concerns all effective locally finite divisors, not just finite polynomial divisors.
proofSteps: Finite-zero interpolation with specified norm inequalities constrains successive coefficient choices to nested closed balls (Lazard Lemmas 4–5 and Proposition 8). Spherical completeness supplies compatible choices when their radii need not tend to zero.
Pass along an exhaustion with the controlled corrections, preserving the exact polynomial divisor rather than allowing extra zeros. Apply the disc argument in both Laurent directions for an annulus.

nodes.title: Bézout and principal closed ideals on open annuli and discs
nodes.statement: If K is spherically complete, A_K(U) is a Bézout domain for any connected nonempty open or half-open annulus or disc U. An ideal is closed iff it is principal. Its nonzero closed ideals are generated by functions realizing their effective divisors. On compact U the stronger PID conclusion holds for any complete K. Principal and finitely generated ideals are closed over any complete K; the spherical hypothesis is needed to turn every divisor ideal into a principal ideal on a noncompact domain.

nodes.title: Closed ideals of the Robba germ ring
nodes.statement: For the parent Robba ring R_K with the final seminorm topology, the only closed ideals are 0 and R_K. This closed-ideal assertion holds over any complete nontrivially nonarchimedean K by the compact-window argument. For spherically complete K the ring is also Bézout by noncompact-analytic-bezout and taking a common chart. Neither assertion says R_K is a field: over Q_p, log(1+t) is nonzero with infinitely many zeros tending to |t|=1, is not a unit, and generates a proper dense ideal.
hypotheses: Closed means closed for the Robba LF topology, not for a single chart or for the Amice norm topology.
The additional Bézout assertion retains spherical completeness; the parent DVR coefficient result is an instance.
proofSteps: Take nonzero f∈I and a chart A_K((r,1)) containing it. On each compact window J_n of an exhaustion, compact preparation gives the finite polynomial zero factor P_n of f. P_n is a unit in the Robba germ ring, since its finitely many nonzero-radius zeros can be excluded by increasing the inner radius. Thus h_n=f/P_n still lies in I and in the original analytic chart, and has no zeros on J_n.

The inverse of h_n on J_n can be approximated arbitrarily well by a Laurent polynomial Q_n. Choose the error so that h_n Q_n→1 on every compact window. Every h_n Q_n lies in I∩A_K((r,1)); continuity of the chart inclusion shows 1 belongs to closure(I) in R_K. This proof uses no spherical completeness.
For finite generators choose a common chart and apply noncompact-analytic-bezout when K is spherically complete, then pass its gcd to the union.
For log(1+t), the zeros ζ_{p^n}−1 have radii tending to 1, so no Robba chart removes all of them. An inverse cannot exist, yet the preceding density result applies to its principal ideal.

sources.match: The Robba ring is Bézout and has only the trivial closed ideals; the wider coefficient closedness assertion here is proved by compact preparation and density.
Compact Laurent approximation and finite zero-factor removal used in the germ proof.

acceptance: For f=t−a with 0<|a|<1, increase the inner radius above |a|; f becomes a unit of R_K.
For log(1+t) over Q_p, the principal ideal is proper but dense, demonstrating why closed ideals do not classify all ideals.
The ideal zero is closed because the chart coefficient functionals separate points and remain continuous for the final seminorm topology.

That cited proof has not been inspected in this pass.

Arabia 1.2.3: lift a finite projective module with a finite free presentation after an étale neighbourhood of I. Lift its residual idempotent ψbar. For principal I=(π), write ψ²−ψ=πα and solve α+(2ψ−1)β+πβ²=0 in matrix coordinates. The Jacobian is invertible modulo π. The solution must commute enough with ψ: the commutator satisfies [ψ,πβ]=πQ[ψ,πβ]; invert det(1−πQ) to force it to vanish. Do not expand noncommuting matrices as if they commuted. Reduce a finitely generated I successively to this case; finite presentation reduces general I to finitely many coefficients. Nakayama supplies a localisation g≡1 modulo I needed to keep the chosen presentation.

Arabia 1.3.1: lift the complete-intersection retract and its projective module, then use the symmetric-algebra presentation and its linear section to lift an arbitrary smooth algebra. Existing nilpotent formal-smooth lifting is insufficient.

In 2.1.2 preserve the two prescribed maps through the symbolic finite-coefficient argument and the product-ideal neighbourhood. In Theorem 2.2.2 use the surjective endpoint map B[T]→B×B with kernel T(T−1). Never cancel π in a ring where π could be a zero divisor.

proofInputs: Use flatness and the mod-π isomorphism to identify every successive π-graded piece and every mod-π^m quotient, hence the completions. For weak surjectivity, lift the chosen mod-π generators and iterate the π-adic error with a degree bound linear in the π-order; the bounds, rather than formal completeness alone, keep the resulting series weakly convergent.

For the relative finite presentation, construct its weak completion on a weak finite presentation over O, verify presentation independence and the universal property. All evaluation/quotient maps extend. An étale neighbourhood preserving mod π is flat, so the collapse applies. It preserves the original maps because the isomorphism is the canonical one.

Include the approximation theorem over a perfect complete field E: for algebraic α and Δ=min_σ v(σα−α), for every ε>0 there exists a∈E with v(α−a)≥Δ−ε. proofInputs: In a finite Galois extension of a perfect base choose c of trace 1. Replacing c by its p-power roots keeps trace 1 and makes its valuation arbitrarily close to zero. Then a=Tr(cα) approximates α, using αTr(c)=α; the manuscript display omits α in that equality.

Approximate a completed invariant x by algebraic α. Every conjugate difference of α becomes arbitrarily small since the action is isometric and fixes x. Apply the approximation theorem and completeness of the perfect base. First pass to completed perfection for imperfect κ.
